summary: Recorded the healed-partition account from receipt 2996ef7e45d946e3bbd6ad696be91ed3 (53 events, exit 0). Its split_result events reproduce the partition outcome of the two earlier receipts, and its healing phase shows convergence of leadership but not of content: comparison 0 holds at parsed index 49 because the cluster ended with exactly one leader, while comparison 1 is violated at the same index because both divergent committed entries were still present, the restarted side's entry in its own store and the other side's in theirs (the two were written at the same index while both sides held the same term, so AppendEntries treats each as a duplicate of the other rather than a conflict); the flag-disabled control holds at parsed index 52 with the single entry that had been committed there. I added a fact for that observation, cited the receipt from the duplicate-skip behaviour as the case where same-index same-term entries with different content both survive, withdrew the limitation that a healed partition was unexercised, and restated the account, keeping explicit that the healing observation covers log stores and leadership only — not what the two state machines hold, nor any later snapshot, election or application-level repair. Remaining boundaries are now the store and fault model alone: disk-backed commit-tracking stores, crash and restart timing, and further repetitions or longer runs.
